Thanks Marissa — great call today. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we kick off formal benchmarking: 

- Primary workload: real-time chat assistant, ~1-3 prompts/user with 200–400 tokens each. Peak concurrency ~250 RPS.
- Our internal SLA target: p95 latency < 250ms for 128-token responses, p99 < 500ms if possible.
- We're comparing Redwood, HyperscaleAI endpoints, and in-house Triton-based serving for cost/latency.

Can you confirm what your expected p95/p99 and tokens/sec numbers look like for a 24k-context model variant? Also interested in batching behavior for short responses.

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear summary, and appreciate the SLA targets. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

Short answers:
- Baseline p95/p99 (128-token resp) on Redwood Hosted using our 24k-context model variant: p95 ~140–220ms, p99 ~360–480ms depending on concurrent load and routing policy.
- Tokens/sec (sustained) per GPU: ~1,800–3,200 tokens/sec for generation-heavy prompts; effective throughput improves with batching and prefix caching.
- For short responses (<=128 tokens) we recommend aggressive KV cache + small auto-batching window (8–12ms) to keep latency predictable.

Key differentiators vs hyperscaler endpoints:
- Deterministic fallback & model variants: we route to lower-latency quantized variants automatically when availability demands — keeps p99 stable.
- Workload-aware batching & KV prefix caching that preserves latency SLOs for chat-like workloads.
- End-to-end observability: per-token cost + p95/p99 breakdowns by route/model.

Proposed next tests (what we ideally run together):
1) A/B run (2 hours each) comparing Redwood Hosted vs HyperscaleAI with your harness and 250 RPS peak ramp: capture p50/p95/p99, error rates, and tokens/sec.
2) Short-response microbench (sustained 128-token responses) to capture p95/p99 at steady state.
3) KV-cache enabled test vs cache-bypass to quantify unit cost improvement and cold-start p95.

Attachments: I attached a short benchmark summary we ran vs a hyperscaler (+ CSV of sample latency traces).

Next steps:
- If you're good, I'll loop in Rishi (SE) and Connor (AE) to schedule the A/B window and get access details for your harness.
- Would you prefer we run the test in US-west region or in your preferred cloud region?

Best,

Hi Sam / Marissa / Connor — thanks for the ping. Confirming Redwood side runbook for Thursday 2026-03-04, 09:00–11:00 PT (US-west):

Test config (summary):
- Model: rwd-24k-v2 (serving variant) — quantized int8 with float16 fallback for long sequences.
- Batching: adaptive batching with 8ms collection window (default) and a forced max batch size of 64 for the A/B.
- KV-cache: test runs with cache enabled (warm-start with 30-minute prefix seeding) vs cache-disabled runs.
- Routing policy: single-region US-west, route preference to low-latency pool; fallback to quantized pool under load.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, error rate, and cost-per-1M-tokens (billing estimator).

Execution steps (what we'll need from Globex):
1) Access: API key for your harness VM and a short-proof workload script (we can run from our side if you'd prefer).
2) Test harness: please share the VM SSH + harness instructions or allow our runner to hit your VM endpoints. We need the same input set for both Redwood and Hyperscale runs.
3) Warmup: 15 minutes steady ramp to target concurrency before each 2-hour window.
4) Data collection: we'll stream latency traces to the shared Drive folder and attach CSV export at the end.

I'll attach the exact curl commands and a one-page runbook to the Drive link by EOD today. If you have any special headers or attribution tokens we should use, send those over.

Notes on expected outcomes (realistic):
- Under a 250 RPS peak with 128-token responses: expect tokens/sec aggregate matching ~200k–600k depending on instance count; per-GPU tokens/sec in the ~2k range as Marissa noted.
- p95 target of <250ms is achievable with KV caching + adaptive batching; p99 will be the differentiator (we tend to see ~360–420ms in similar customer runs when fallback behavior is constrained).

We'll also compute cost delta vs hyperscaler (including egress + per-token) and highlight where quantized variants reduce cost but may slightly widen p99.

I'll be online 8:30am PT Thursday for a quick sync and will post the runbook to the Drive.

Cheers,
